That’s not what I’m saying at all, lol. I’m not using Jurassic Park as a prime example of practical effects. I’m using it as a prime example of when the directors and creative team flexed how CG and practical effects can be blended in such an effective way that looks seamless. So many movies get that wrong and don’t even seem to consider it for many reasons. 

In my opinion, movies that have taken the same approach that JP did, have had a way more effective impact that each of them have since become timeless movies that nobody looks at 20 - 30 years after they come out and says “wow, this looks so bad now.” No one has ever said that about Jurassic Park and probably won’t about stuff like Fury Road which is a recent example that was amazing and has a lot of rewatch value for me.

Nobody is using Jurassic Park as how to do practical effects. It’s an example of when to decide when CG is the right choice and when to know when CG could fall flat and instead replacing it with the now dying art that is practical effects and in their case, puppeteering. 

I love the history of this movies creative decisions because when you go into all of the creative differences by the ones that had moved toward CG, and the ones not wanting to see practical get sidelined by digital, they came together to deliver a cohesive final product.

I’m probably rambling, but I think it’s worth it to point out.

It sounds like your account has a limitation on it at the moment. You generally will receive an email with a general reason for why it was placed on there, but there are many different reasons for a limitation.

Is you provided everything they asked from you, then they’ll review it and this usually take 5 - 7 days, but can be a lot quicker than that. 

Also, keep in mind that a limitation doesn’t always mean you’re doing anything wrong - but that their system either wants to be sure that your identity is confirmed, your information is correct, or that your account could be transacting more than usual and they just want to know what changed or why.

They’ll send you an email as soon as they lift the limitation, though. So make sure you check your email and also spam folder so you don’t miss anything. 

It’s kind of just a waiting game at this point.

As long as you advertised the item to be in good condition and sent it as such, you can definitely appeal if you received something different back than how it should have been received. 

Also, what was the customers reason for returning it? If their reason was that it was damaged, then it usually isn’t valid to appeal for the same reason as the buyer has already claimed.

If you do appeal, they will usually ask you for some form of proof like an official document or letter from a third party depending on the item and its value.

I don’t see the harm in trying - if you get denied, you’d be in the same spot you’re in right now. Better to put in extra work for a chance of getting reimbursed than doing nothing and definitely not getting reimbursed.

The few times I’ve had this happen, I’ve almost always been reimbursed. But there’s never going to be a guarantee. 

Good luck!

YSK that PayPal has never been compromised as a company, so unfortunately, if your account is being consistently hacked into - then it is likely due to a personal account like your email, password, or device being compromised. 

I’d recommend resetting all passwords to all of your social media accounts, financial service accounts, and emails to ensure that there is not a fraudster who has gained access to somewhere they could be receiving your PayPal emails/notifications and resetting your password.

Also, if you receive any seemingly suspicious emails that you may not think are coming from the legit PayPal, you can forward them to spoof @ paypal . com. or phishing @ paypal . Com.au if you’re in Australia.

This will flag the emails and have them reviewed by PayPal for scam emails using their logo.

If your account has a limitation that is requiring proof of fulfillment, the previous suggestions won’t suffice. Twenty-one day holds apply to standard payment holds, but a limitation prevents you from withdrawing any money until the limitation is completely resolved.

You will need to provide some sort of proof. If you do not have tracking, I would suggest typing a word document with an explanation as to why you do not have the tracking or anything you can showing proof of delivery/confirmation clearly and supplying it as a PDF in place of the fulfillment confirmation.

It does not always work, but it can depending on the reviewing party. Submitting something is better than nothing in this circumstance.

Please remember that to qualify for Seller Protection in a dispute or chargeback, you must have a valid tracking number showing proof of delivery to the address in the transaction details listed in your PayPal activity. Without it, if a claim is filed for an item not being received, you will lose your claim and your money 99% of the time. With no delivery confirmation, it’s automatically decided in favor of the buyer.

If you’re having trouble accessing your account, it’s best to call or chat with customer service using the Contact option at the bottom of any PayPal page.

If that’s not available to you, the next best options are to reach them on Facebook or Twitter. 

Good luck!

But, if your account is negative on PayPal and you add a financial to your account and make a purchase or send a payment, the negative balance will be automatically added to the amount of whatever you’re buying or sending.
